item.title: Fixing Eclipse Startup Failure: Java Bitness Mismatch Issues
item.description:
“Fixing Eclipse Startup Failure: Java Bitness Mismatch Issues”

When attempting to launch Eclipse, encountering errors like “Java was started but returned exit code=13” frequently points toward an incompatibility between the Eclipse application’s architecture (32-bit or 64-bit) and the Java Runtime Environment (JRE) or Java Development Kit (JDK) it is attempting to use. How can developers systematically diagnose and resolve this common Java/Eclipse configuration friction?

The core issue often stems from Eclipse launching with a 32-bit JVM when the Eclipse executable itself is 64-bit, or vice-versa. On 64-bit Windows installations, 32-bit applications are typically directed to C:\Program Files (x86)\, while 64-bit applications reside in C:\Program Files\.
